insights.headline: Gold steadies near $3,645 after Monday's sharp rebound as bargain hunters return
insights.summary: Spot gold edged up 0.4% to $3,645.29 in early Asian trade on Tuesday, extending Monday's rebound from a 14-month low, while silver rose 1.2% to $43.55. On MCX, gold held near Rs 1.24 lakh per 10 g and silver above Rs 1.51 lakh per kg after Monday's 2.4% gains. The next test is Wednesday's US core PCE inflation data, due at 19:00 IST, ahead of the Fed's 9 December decision.
points: Spot gold $3,645.29, up 0.4% in Asia, extending Monday's rebound of more than 3% from a 14-month low.
Silver $43.55, up 1.2% in Asia; MCX silver above Rs 1.51 lakh per kg after Monday's 2.45% gain.
MCX gold near Rs 1.24 lakh per 10 g after a 2.38% rise on Monday; silver gained 2.45% to Rs 1,51,435 per kg.
Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, lifting equities and steadying the AI-led selloff.
Next test: US core PCE on Wednesday at 19:00 IST, ahead of the Fed's 9 December decision.

brief.headline: Gold extends rebound as bargain hunters return
brief.summary: Spot gold rose to $3,645 after Monday's 3% rebound, MCX gold near Rs 1.24 lakh per 10 g; inflation data due Wednesday.

bullets.text: Bargain hunting after last week's selloff, a steadier dollar and Nvidia's CEO return steadied risk appetite, Reuters and Kitco report.
MCX gold held near Rs 1.24 lakh per 10 g and silver above Rs 1.51 lakh per kg; trade bodies link falling imports to PM Modi's appeal.
Watch Wednesday: US core PCE at 19:00 IST, the next test for the rebound ahead of the Fed's 9 December decision.

trending.title: Rebound holds into Tuesday as bargain hunters return
trending.summary: Spot gold edged up to $3,645 in Asian trade after Monday's climb of more than 3% from a 14-month low, with traders watching whether the recovery survives Wednesday's US inflation data.

trending.title: Silver's slide still runs deeper than gold's
trending.summary: Silver holds near $43.20 after crashing to a 14-month low of $40.78 last week; FXStreet notes the bounce looks technical, with a December Fed hike now fully priced.

trending.title: Trade bodies credit Modi appeal for import slide
trending.summary: Trade bodies say PM Modi's appeal to limit non-essential gold buying cut imports sharply, saving $16.46 billion over seven months; the data behind the claim is debated.

trending.title: Next test: US core PCE on Wednesday
trending.summary: Traders look to Wednesday's US core PCE print at 19:00 IST for the next cue on Fed rates, ahead of the Fed's decision due 9 December.

trending.title: Cheaper silver revives Salem's anklet workshops
trending.summary: Salem's silver anklet makers say orders have recovered to nearly half of normal levels as silver fell to about Rs 175 a gram, with workshops running nearly six days a week ahead of Pongal.

items.title: Gold, silver prices see sharp rebounds as AI shares rally, renewed Fed uncertainty
items.summary: Spot gold traded near $3,635.10 an ounce late Monday, up 2.75%, and silver around $43.02, up about 4.6%, as bargain hunting and improving risk sentiment lifted metals after last week's selloff, Kitco reports. Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive, steadying equities, though Fed tightening concerns, high Treasury yields and geopolitical uncertainty still challenge the recovery.

items.title: Gold edges up on bargain buying after selloff; US inflation data awaited
items.summary: Spot gold rose 0.4% to $3,645.29 an ounce in early Asian trade, extending Monday's rebound from a 14-month low, while silver climbed 1.2% to $43.55. Markets now await Wednesday's US PCE inflation data, with traders pricing a 95% chance of a December Fed rate rise.

items.title: Gold prices jump 3% as bargain hunting overshadows slowing U.S. manufacturing and services activity
items.summary: Spot gold jumped more than 3% to $3,668.20 an ounce as bargain hunting after last week's selloff outweighed soft US data, Kitco reports. S&P Global's flash composite PMI fell to 54.6 in November from 55.9, a four-month low, with manufacturing at 54.5 and services at 54.7, the latter missing forecasts. The gold market barely reacted to the data, with the rebound driven by dip-buying.

items.title: Gold Rebounds as Huang's Return to Nvidia Revives Risk Appetite
items.summary: Gold extended its rebound after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive, rising as much as 4.3% to $3,690 an ounce after a near-9% slide last week. Bloomberg reports the selling was concentrated in futures, while ETF holdings stayed steady, according to UBS, and retail dip-buying emerged in Shenzhen jewellery markets. Fed officials still back higher rates to fight sticky inflation.

MCX December gold futures rose Rs 2,899, or 2.38%, to Rs 1,24,677 per 10 grams as speculators built fresh positions on firm spot demand, PTI reported; silver futures gained 2.45% to Rs 1,51,435 per kg. In New York, gold futures rose 2.14% to $3,614.25 an ounce and silver futures 2.91%.
items.title: Gold futures rise to Rs 1.24 lakh per 10 grams, silver crosses Rs 1.51 lakh per kg
Domestic stock markets closed for Guru Nanak Jayanti; MCX to resume trading in evening session
items.summary: MCX will stay shut for its morning session on Tuesday for Guru Nanak Jayanti, with gold and silver futures trading resuming in the evening session from 5 pm; NSE and BSE are closed for the day and reopen on Wednesday.

MCX gold futures rose 2.2% and silver 2.11% on Monday after last week's slide — gold fell 11% and silver 16.2% on the week — as short covering and bargain buying met a softer dollar and fading bets on Fed hikes. Spot gold traded near $3,609, up 2%, and silver just above $42. Analysts quoted remain cautious, saying the rebound must hold above resistance to confirm a turn.
items.title: Gold and silver rebound over 2% after steep weekly losses: Can the recovery sustain?
Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD grips recovery above $43; outlook remains cautious
items.summary: Silver held near $43.20 in Asian trade, keeping its recovery after last week's slide to a 14-month low of $40.78, but FXStreet notes the bounce looks technical — driven by oversold indicators, not a shift in outlook — as markets price a full December Fed hike and about 70% odds of one in January. The revival in AI stocks could further dull precious metals' appeal.

items.title: Salem Anklet manufacturers see a silver lining as metal price dips Rs 2L/ kg in 10 months
items.summary: Salem's silver anklet makers say orders have recovered to nearly half of normal levels after more than a year of sluggish business, as silver fell to about Rs 175 a gram in the city from Rs 195 a week ago, the article reports. Workshops that ran about two days a week now work nearly six days a week ahead of Pongal.

items.title: Silver Price Drops Below US$50 — What Matters Now for Miners and Explorers?
items.summary: Silver has fallen below $50 an ounce and now trades around the $43 level after crashing from a record above $120 in January, the Investing News Network reports. Silver company executives are split on what comes next, with some concerned about further declines and others seeing a buying opportunity after the sharp correction.

items.title: Indian rupee could rise to 91.50/$ on equity inflows, HDFC Bank's treasury head says
items.summary: The rupee could strengthen to 91.50 per dollar if strong equity inflows continue, HDFC Bank treasury head Arup Rakshit said, seeing it in a 91.50-93.50 range near term. The currency closed Friday at 92.67, up nearly 2.5% in November on record $12 billion of foreign equity inflows, and Rakshit expects the RBI to raise rates in December, with a 25-basis-point hike more or less given.

items.title: Did PM Modi's appeal really bring down gold prices? Here's what the data shows
items.summary: Mathrubhumi tests the PM's claim that his appeal to avoid non-essential gold purchases lowered prices: 24-carat gold fell about 18% from Rs 15,250 a gram on 9 May to Rs 12,523 on 21 November. The piece concludes the appeal alone cannot explain it — the import duty rose from 6% to 15% in May, imports fell about 40% in April–October, and a stronger dollar and Fed hike expectations also weighed.

items.title: PM Modi's appeal to avoid gold purchases reflects in import data, India saves $16.46 billion in 7 months: CAIT
items.summary: India's gold import bill fell nearly 40% to $24.78 billion in April–October 2026 from $41.24 billion a year earlier, saving $16.46 billion, the Confederation of All India Traders says, crediting PM Modi's appeal to avoid non-essential gold purchases. October imports fell 62.6% to $5.51 billion from $14.72 billion a year earlier.
